minutes_text:
MINUTES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  AUGUST 28, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
A special meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 6:20 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City
Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Griggs, Harik, Martin, Nilsen, Shinn,
  Schachter, and Ciarolla (arrived at 6:52 pm)
  Committee Members Absent:  Medawar and Silvano
  City Staff Present:  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 22, 2023
  MEMBER GRIGGS moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN to:
  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 22, 2023, EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHACHTER so ordered.
5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA
  NONE.
6.  BUSINESS ITEMS
A.  DISCUSSION OF E-BIKES ON BRIDLE TRAILS (VERBAL REPORT)
  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that complaints had been received regarding e-bikes
  on bridle trails and that there have been issues with youth on e-bikes at Ernie
  Howlett Park. She reported that Staff met with the Sheriff’s Department to discuss
  the issue and that Sheriff's deputies have been patrolling trail heads and parks.
  She shared that the Sheriff’s Posse has also assisted on the bridle trails when
  available, but that due to scheduling issues they are not currently available to
  assist.

  1
 Supervisor Pinuelas also discussed signage, noting existing signage on the bridle
trails, but reported that Staff is adding signage that will be posted to A-frames so
they are moveable and can be placed in areas where attention is needed. She also
noted that Staff would be working on outreach to the schools and will work with the
Sheriff Department to develop messaging for students and parents. Supervisor
Pinuelas also shared that Staff had received inquiries regarding issuing citations
and that Staff was working with the Sheriff's deputies to see if or how that could be
conducted since the issues involve minors whose guardians are not present with
them at the time of the violation.
CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that in the past the City had a code enforcement
officer who was able to issue citations but that she believed special training was
needed. She added that recruitment was in process and inquired about the
possibility of the new code enforcement officer having the ability to issue citations.
MEMBER SHINN stated that she felt something drastic needed to be done. She
discussed a recent equestrian injury resulting from an e-bike rider on a trail. She
requested that the City put a sign on Crenshaw at the beginning and end of the
trail and suggested increasing fines to $2,000 or $5,000.
MEMBER SHINN inquired about the fine for riding bikes on the trails. Supervisor
Pinuelas stated that she could not recollect if an administrative fine would apply or
another fine based on violating the code, but that she would look into it.
MEMBER HARIK stated that since e-bikes are relatively new, she could see the
need for a new rule or change to the code to address them. Supervisor Pinuelas
stated that there is a regulation in the Code prohibiting wheeled vehicles on bridle
trails.
MEMBER SHINN stated that it would be difficult to stop cyclists and enforce a
violation, and asked if photos could be taken of violators. Supervisor Pinuelas
explained that there may be laws in place limiting the ability to take photos of
violators, but she would inquire with the Sheriff Department.
MEMBER SHINN asked if the City could use banners to educate the public, add
new regulations to the code and include a fine. She reiterated the need for a large
fine to deter violators.
CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that schools are concerned about the issue as well,
so working with the schools to educate would be positive and concurred with
MEMBER SHINN that a fine would be a deterrent.
MEMBER GRIGGS suggested a bike license could be a requirement to ride an e-
bike in the City that way cyclists go through an education course that teaches the
rules and lets them know they cannot ride on the bridle trails.

  2
 MEMBER HARIK stated that there was a similar program here in the past and that
youth had to wait until the third grade to be able to take the class and then received
a decal with an assigned number for their bikes.
MEMBER GRIGGS stated that there is signage in front of the Masongate bridle
trail that states no motor vehicles are allowed, but vehicles are seen driving to
backyard barns and people bring children in strollers on the trails. She stated
cyclists travel through there because it is a short cut and signs are not working.
CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that the City of Palos Verdes Estates is also
concerned about this issue and that they have motorized carts that their law
enforcement uses on the trails. She added that there was a donation of carts to
Palos Verdes Estates Police Department which may be a helpful option for RHE
law enforcement or Code Enforcement.
MEMBER BRTIS stated that she thought scooters were just as bad because they
ride along sidewalks and then take off along the bridle trail frequently jumping off
the sidewalk.
MEMBER SHINN asked if all bike riders could be required to take a course. CHAIR
SCHACHTER responded that enforcement would be difficult.
MEMBER HARIK stated it is an issue that goes across the board everywhere
including the beach cities.
Audience Member Sharon Yarber stated it would be good to have this discussion
at the City Council level with City Attorney present and talk to Sheriff because she
is not sure what can be done legally and what impediments there are. She
commented on the existing ordinance which says wheeled vehicles are not allowed
on the bridle trails and that it would need to be amended to add a fine and that she
thought a fine was appropriate. She also commented that she thought dummy
cameras should be placed on the bridle trails as a deterrent and that she believed
that the Sheriff could cite minors. She suggested somehow getting the Posse
members authorized to give citations since they ride on the bridle trails where they
can cite violators. She said currently the Posse can only educate but are seeing
patterns of day and times of this activity. She suggested having Sheriff stationed
in a couple key areas to issue citations and fines and that word would spread. She
also shared that she attended a townhall held by Assemblymember Muratsuchi
which included an e-bike discussion and thinks the City should work with other
local cities to create legislation at state level that says you have to be at least age
16 or 14 to ride an e-bike or have a license.
Ms. Yarber stated that as an equestrian she is focusing on the bridle trails, but the
issues expand broader than the trails.
CHAIR SCHACHTER acknowledged Ms. Yarber and said that the issue could be
discussed with the City Manager and the Assistant City Manager to request that it

  3
 be put on a Peninsula Public Safety Committee agenda to be discussed, but would
still have to go to City Council for initial discussion.
MEMBER SHINN asked if there were a lot of bike shops on the hill that sell e-
bikes. MEMBER GRIGGS noted there is one in the City. MEMBER SHINN
suggested giving them a poster that informs that e-bikes are not permitted on the
bridle trails.
Audience Member Charlene O’Neil stated that this is a safety issue and referenced
an incident in the Conservancy area. She added that she thinks everyone needs
to take it seriously.
CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if the Committee Members wanted to make a motion
to take the issue to the City Council or if they wanted to do more research first and
stated that she understood time was of the essence. She added that another
consideration could be to try to get the cities to coordinate.
MEMBER SHINN recommended the Committee make a motion to bring
awareness to the City Council of the situation even though the research has not
been done yet but that everyone knows what is going on and could be done later
and felt the issue shouldn’t be delayed.
MEMBER BRTIS concurred that it should be put on the agenda right away. She
added that it’s not just the bridle trails and that is just as much the sidewalks and
everywhere.
MEMBER MARTIN stated that it is a general safety issue and asked at what point
is it no longer a bike and considered a motorcycle where they should have a license
because the bikes are getting faster and faster.
Supervisor Pinuelas shared that Carlsbad has something in place that when a child
gets cited for their first offense, they can take a safety course in lieu of paying a
fine.
CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that if the Committee is requesting it be put on a
Council agenda that having a good turnout was critical. MEMBER SHINN stated
that the word could be put out to the equestrians. CHAIR SCHACTHER stated it
would be done to raise consciousness and then from there Staff could be asked to
research the different components.
MEMBER HARIK made a motion for the e-bike discussion to be put on a future
City Council agenda.
MEMBER GRIGGS requested the motion be amended to include amending the
existing code regarding wheeled vehicles to add e-bikes specifically with an
associated fine.

  4
 MEMBER SHINN stated they could include the need for licensing, training and
everything discussed.
CHAIR SCHACHTER stated the next Council meeting was September 12 in
response to MEMBER SHINN.
MEMBER HARIK asked if the Committee could send an email if the item would be
on the agenda. Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed.
MEMBER SHINN stated she could work to get the word out to the equestrians and
would let Gil Houle know to inform those at the city stables. Ms. Yarber stated they
would inform the PVPHA members.
CHAIR SCHACHTER asked for a roll call
MEMBER SHINN made a motion, amended and seconded by MEMBER GRIGGS
TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:
  TO BRING AWARNESS TO THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE E-BIKE ISSUE
  AND RECOMMEND THEY DISCUSS IT AND TO RECOMMEND THE
  EXISITING CODE REGARDING THE PROHIBITION OF WHEELED
  VEHICLES ON BRIDLE TRAILS BE AMENDED TO INCLUDE E-BIKES
  SPECIFICALLY WITH A FINE RELATED TO E-BIKES.
  AYES:  Brtis, Harik, Martin, Nielson, Griggs, Schachter
  ABSENT:  Ciarolla, Medawar, Silvano
** MEMBER CIAROLLA arrived at 6:52 pm.**
MEMBER CIAROLLA stated that she researched DMV restrictions regarding e-
bikes and learned they are not supposed to be ridden on streets by children under
age 16 and that they must wear helmets at all times. She asked why this is an
issue stating they do not belong on the horse trails.
Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Sheriff enforces it if they see it because
wheeled vehicles are not allowed on the bridle trails.
CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that the issue is how to enforce it and that the City
is in the process of hiring a new code enforcement officer. She said that if the
code enforcement officer could write tickets that could be one way to enforce it in
response to MEMBER CIAROLLA. CHAIR SCHACHTER added that the Lomita
Sheriff does not patrol bridle trails but if we could investigate the times and places
on the trials and ask them to be at specific locations to enforce it that could help.
MEMBER CIAROLLA asked if the issues are mostly on Palos Verdes Drive North
because of the schools along the Drive. CHAIR SCHACHTER responded that she
could not speak to that and MEMBER SHINN responded that they are at Ernie
Howlett parking lot and on the landfill. CHAIR SCHACHTER referenced the

  5
   Equestrian Issues Log which included e-bike issues. MEMBER CIAROLLA stated
  that she was aware of the need to report issues so it can be logged but asked if
  there was something else that could be done.
  MEMBER HARIK responded that there is a need to work at the grass roots level
  to get something done because it is a problem everywhere. She stated that it is
  not just on the horse trails and there is a need for the Committee to bring it to the
  City Council.
  MEMBER SHINN asked if Sheriff Deputies could be advised of the location of
  landfill is, so they are aware when notified of issues on the landfill. Supervisor
  Pinuelas affirmed. MEMBER SHINN noted that there are a lot of new Deputies
  and that she gave a class at the landfill years ago.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER thanked the Committee for all their input and said
  Supervisor Pinuelas would let the Committee know when the item is put on the
  City Council agenda.
B.  SHARING THE TRAILS SAFETY OUTREACH VIDEO SERIES UPDATE
  (VERBAL REPORT)
  Supervisor Pinuelas shared that a videographer had been secured and that she
  would contact the Committee members who volunteered to participate to
  coordinate scheduling.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER shared that Susan Robinson had moved and would be
  missed. She noted that she had volunteered to assist with the video related to
  dogs but thought others would be able to help.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that one of the videos would be related to bikes and
  that it would make sense that it focusses on e-bikes but would cover all bikes.
C.  BUSINESS LICENSING REQUIREMENTS
  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a verbal overview per written report.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER noted the examples provided in the report and stated that it
  is not cost prohibitive and, in some cases, based on percentage of income, adding
  that the examples give a good idea of how much individuals would pay.
  MEMBER SHINN asked if real estate agents needed to pay for a license each
  year. Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed and stated that all businesses are required to
  have a license.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER affirmed that veterinarians receive a license also in
  response to an additional question by MEMBER SHINN and added that farriers
  should receive a license which is based on a percentage of their income that
  comes from that service within the City.

  6
 Supervisor Pinuelas noted that while there is not a specific listing for veterinarians,
their business falls into the professional category. She added that every business
conducting service in the City is required to have a license even if that business is
not located in the City.
Supervisor Pinuelas explained that if the City is informed that someone does not
have a business license, the business is contacted to inform them of the
requirement and given information regarding how to acquire a license in response
to MEMBER SHINN.
MEMBER CIAROLLA noted that she does not think any of the farriers have
business licenses and that she was not aware if the veterinarians do.
Supervisor Pinuelas noted that there is a veterinarian with a business license, but
that Committee Members could contact her to inquire about specific veterinarians
to see if they have a license or can look it up on the website.
MEMBER SHINN asked if Amazon would need a license. MEMBER MARTIN
responded that the contractors they hire to make the deliveries would. Supervisor
Pinuelas noted that anyone conducting business in the City needs a license.
MEMBER BRTIS stated that she passes the little league fields and batting cages
and sees people providing lessons. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that is not
allowed and that Staff does what they can to enforce it but that it is a challenge to
enforce.
CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that she thinks it is hard to enforce for those who don’t
have a physical space and drive in and out of the City, not just for those using City
facilities but those who conduct business into private yards.
MEMBER SHINN noted that a lot of gardeners have licenses.
CHAIR SCHACHTER appreciated having the information, knowing where
equestrian related businesses fall on the schedule, and that specific fees did not
need to be developed for them as they were for horse trainers. She added that she
thought the farriers and veterinarians were probably generating more revenue than
the trainers who are paying for licenses and fees.
MEMBER CIAROLLA noted that the trainers use City facilities while the
veterinarians do not. CHAIR SCHACHTER affirmed and added that that they are
operating business within the City.
CHAIR SCHACHTER noted that having the information and being aware of it is
helpful and that the Committee Members could educate those they conduct
business with.
Supervisor Pinuelas stated that education has been the City’s approach to
enforcement in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER. She added that the Committee

  7
   could let her know of businesses that do not have a license and that Staff would
  reach out to them.
  RECEIVED AND FILED.
D.  DISCUSSION OF COMMITTEE MEETING TIME (VERBAL REPORT)
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the idea of starting the Equestrian Committee
  meetings earlier was proposed and was being presented to the Committee for
  consideration. She stated that the Committee could consider moving the start time
  up from 7:00 pm to 6:00 pm and that if a majority of the Committee was interested
  in doing so, Staff would look into the process to do that.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked the Committee if it would be more problematic to get
  to a 6:00 pm meeting.
  MEMBER CIAROLLA stated that she believed it is difficult for people who work
  and those who need to get families settled before attending. She added that getting
  to the Park and Activities 6:00 pm meetings in the summer can be difficult at times.
  MEMBER GRIGGS stated she had to leave work early to make it to that evening’s
  meeting.
  MEMBER HARIK stated that she could meet earlier but noted that she works very
  close by and the frequency of the meetings is not often enough to be an issue.
  MEMBER CIAROLLA noted that other meetings such as Park and Activities and
  City Council meetings start at 7:00 pm, and that it is easier when everything starts
  at the same time.
  MEMBER SHINN stated that she prefers a 7:00 pm start time but could do what
  the majority prefers.
  MEMBER NIELSEN concurred with MEMBER SHINN and noted she had to make
  arrangements for the 6:00 pm start time but that it would be more of an issue if the
  Committee met more frequently. She stated that she could make either work but
  had a preference for the 7:00 pm start time.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that she brought up the idea because the Traffic and
  Safety Committee starts at 6:00 pm but if the 7:00 pm start time works there is no
  need to change it.
E.  AMBASSADOR PROGRAM SUBCOMMITTEE (VERBAL REPORT)
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Susan Robinson’s resignation from the Equestrian
  Committee created an opening on the Ambassador Program Subcommittee. She
  stated that the subcommittee now has only one member and asked if there was
  interest from any of the Committee members to join the subcommittee. Supervisor

  8
   Pinuelas added that there was nothing to report regarding the program plans at
  that time.
  MEMBER SHINN suggested the program be put on hold due to the timing of the
  City Celebration and the e-bike issue. She furthered that it is a great idea and that
  she thinks it should be kept on the list, adding that the future program volunteers
  could potentially assist with the e-bike issue and education.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that it is still on the list to be developed and noted that
  the subcommittee would likely not meet until November. She noted that the horse
  safety video series and the e-bike issue would take priority but the Ambassador
  Program would continue to be on the list.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER suggested the item be readdressed at the end of the year
  or the beginning of next year to allow time to address the other issues as they
  move forward and allow time to see if the program can be dovetailed with the
  education regarding e-bikes and the safety video series.
  Supervisor Pinuelas asked if there was any interest at that time in joining the
  subcommittee. CHAIR SCHACHTER and MEMBER MARTIN volunteered to join
  the subcommittee.
6.  STAFF ITEMS
A.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  MEMBER HARIK stated there were issues on the Nature Trail as a result of the
  winds noting downed trees blocking the trail.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated she spoke with Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith and appreciates that the log documents not only issues reported but
  also documents work being done related to both the parks and the bridle trails.

B.  CITY CELEBRATION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the City Celebration plans noting it
  would take place on Saturday, September 23 from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm at the Empty
  Saddle Club. She reported that Staff was still soliciting sponsorships and the event
  had three sponsors to date including Waste Management, Peninsula Heritage
  School, and All Kidz Urgent Care. She reported that new activities geared towards
  older youth were planned such as inflatable axe throwing and guided horse rides.
  She noted that the event would have one pony sweep instead of two with the
  addition of the guided horse rides for older children.

  MEMBER MARTIN stated the guided horse rides would take place between the
  roping arena and the Torrance boundary, where practice trial courses are done in
  response CHAIR SCHACHTER. He added that cars are not allowed in that area.

  9
 Supervisor Pinuelas stated that face painting was being brought back this year and
that based on feedback from last year, a second corn pit would be added to the
event. She noted that one would be designated for younger children up to age 4
and the other for older children ages 5-10. Supervisor Pinuelas reported that
mailing of the event flyer was in process to residents and that it includes free
passes for two activities.

CHAIR SCHACHTER inquired about the Equestrian events. MEMBER MARTIN
provided information in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER regarding equestrian
events.

Ms. O’Neil stated that the PVPHA was gathering prizes for the Raffle Ride but it
had been slow and that they needed more prizes.

MEMBER SHINN let the Committee Members know that they could ask for
donations at restaurants they frequent and shared that she was doing that and
asking for gift cards from other businesses she frequents.

Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff has a letter that can be provided to donors
that includes Pepper Tree Foundation information and the tax identification number
for their donations.

Supervisor Pinuelas affirmed that she could email the letter to Ms. O’Neil and to
the Committee in response to Ms. O’Neil and MEMBER SHINN.

Ms. O'Neil stated that Melody Colbert sent an email regarding the city ordinance
pertaining to wheeled vehicles not being allowed on the trail and asked why that
couldn’t be exercised.

Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the issue is citing minors and that the challenge is
enforcing it and citing without the parents present and that is what staff is working
with the Sheriff to figure out.

Ms. O’Neil stated that she heard it often occurs after school and in the landfill area.
Supervisor Pinuelas stated she would share that with the Sheriffs.

Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Sheriff’s Posse is booked but that she would
share it with the Sheriff’s deputies as staff is informing them when there are issues
at the park and that they were able to post a radio car at one of the trail heads in
response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

CHAIR SCHACHTER asked Ms. O’Neil who should be given the Raffle Ride
donations. Ms. O'Neil said they should be given to Melody Colbert. Supervisor
Pinuelas shared that the Committee Members could give donations to Staff and
that Staff would let the subcommittee know and get the items to Melody Colbert.

  10
   MEMBER SHINN and MEMBER MARTIN discussed who was volunteering for the
  Equestrian events and MEMBER SHINN stated another volunteer was needed at
  the gate in response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

  MEMBER MARTIN said he would work with the DJ regarding the sound equipment
  in response to MEMBER SHINN’s comments about the issues experienced last
  year.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER offered to assist with the event and inquired about the
  schedule. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that the Jr. Drill Team would lead the
  flag salute at 12:00 pm followed by the Mayor’s welcome.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated the volleyball game would take place at 10:00 am in
  response to CHAIR SCHACHTER.

C.  EQUESTRIAN RECOGNITION UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that the plaques for both Carol Dean Porter and Jan
  Ball would be ordered the following week and that the bench for Jan Ball had
  already been ordered. She stated she would be reaching out to the Committee
  once plans for the dedications had been set.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if it was possible to have both dedications on the
  same day. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that she thought that could be done
  and would work towards that.

D.  WASTE MANAGEMENT ROUTE CHANGES EFFECTIVE JULY 31, 2023
  (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported on the route changes and explained they were done
  in an effort to enhance service and reduce truck traffic and road impacts. She noted
  that the City and Waste Management collaborated to modify the schedule and that
  residents could contact Waste Management or City staff with any questions.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated she believed manure pickup stayed the same.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated the changes were only made to residential waste,
  recycling, and green organic waste.

E.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas reported that Peartree Lane updates were being posted
  regularly on the City website at RHE.city/Peartree. She reported that the Rotary
  Club was organizing donation efforts for those affected and information could also
  be found on that page. She stated that the HOA retained a geologist who was
  doing an assessment, but nothing had been identified to date. She also reported
  that the City recently worked with LA County’s Urban Search and Rescue who did

  11
   household hazardous waste retrieval and were able to retrieve some personal
  items at the same time. She said those interested in updates could subscribe by
  going to the website.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER asked if the Committee Members were subscribed to the
  newsletter and explained how to sign up. She stated that it goes out biweekly
  and that it is informative and includes information about the hazardous waste
  removal at Peartree.
  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that the newsletters are also used to educate. She
  said she had spoken to the City Manager who said information regarding e-bikes
  would also be included in the newsletters.

8.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  MEMBER HARIK stated there are trees down on the Nature Trail at the George F
  Canyon Nature Center.

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that the Fern Creek Trail down to Ernie Howlett is still
  very overgrown and that it is getting very narrow.

B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  MEMBER SHINN asked if a Sheriff could come out to the next meeting. She stated
  that she would like to go over some of the safety items that may have been
  forgotten such as ensuring they carry halters and ropes and making sure they
  know how to get to different places such as the City stables and the landfill so they
  can be more aware. She explained that she has called dispatch, and they are
  unaware of those locations.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated that it is important to get the right person to the
  meeting. She noted that a Deputy had attended the Traffic and Safety Committee
  meetings and that it had been very helpful and informative.

  MEMBER CIAROLLA stated they should also know how to get down to the
  preserve.

  CHAIR SCHACHTER stated it should probably be the Captain and asked Staff to
  find out who should attend.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  12
 CHAIR SCHACHTER stated the next meeting was scheduled for September 23.
MEMBER BRTIS stated that Yom Kippur was on that date. Supervisor Pinuelas
stated that the meeting could be rescheduled due to the holiday. CHAIR
SCHACHTER recommended the next meeting take place after City Celebration as
opposed to before. CHAIR SCHACHTER noted that it would likely be in October
